title: A candidate asks. The team stays connected.
intro: Follow Amaka's interview question from her candidate view to a prepared panel and a clear next step.
prompt: Should I prepare a presentation for the panel interview?

frames.label: Ask
frames.heading: The question has somewhere to go.
frames.body: Amaka asks about preparation. Her recruiter sees the question alongside the role and interview stage.

message.author: Amaka
message.text: Should I prepare a presentation, or will we discuss my experience?

frames.outcome: The recruiter has the question and its context.

frames.label: Reply
frames.activity: Recruiter response shared in the sample
frames.heading: A useful answer, not another status.
frames.body: The recruiter checks the brief and replies. Amaka knows what to prepare and can continue the conversation.

message.author: Tunde, recruiter
message.text: No presentation needed. Please bring an example of improving an operations process. What would you like us to clarify?

frames.outcome: Amaka can prepare and reply in the same conversation.

frames.label: Interview
frames.heading: Different perspectives. One shared role.
frames.body: After the sample interview, HR checks the panel's structured feedback and identifies the contribution still outstanding.

message.author: Tunde, recruiter
message.text: People and technical feedback are available. Chidi, please add your operations evidence before our review.

frames.outcome: The missing contribution has a named owner.

frames.label: Review
frames.heading: The team decides with the evidence.
frames.body: The completed panel feedback and candidate conversation come together. The hiring manager owns the decision and next communication.

message.author: Chidi, hiring manager
message.text: Let's review the evidence together, agree our next step and keep Amaka informed.

frames.outcome: A human-led decision with a clear follow-up owner.

manual.title: When the conversation is scattered
manual.outcome: The team has to reconnect the story.

title: Make Zainab's first week feel considered.
intro: Watch a new joiner's welcome move from assigned tasks to introductions, a first goal and a manager check-in.
prompt: What should I focus on before my first manager check-in?

frames.label: Prepare
frames.heading: A plan before the first morning.
frames.body: HR and Zainab's manager agree the essentials. Each task has an owner instead of becoming a general welcome email.

message.author: Ada, people partner
message.text: Welcome, Zainab. Start with your role brief. Your manager will help you connect each task to the team's work.

frames.outcome: Zainab knows where to begin and who can help.

frames.label: Begin
frames.heading: The checklist starts a conversation.
frames.body: Zainab reviews the brief and raises a practical question. Her manager can respond before the first goal is agreed.

message.author: Zainab
message.text: I've read the brief. Could we walk through a real handover before I choose my first improvement task?

frames.outcome: The welcome responds to the person, not just the checklist.

frames.label: Connect
frames.heading: Meet the people behind the process.
frames.body: The manager connects Zainab with the team and a practical learning task. The first check-in now has a useful focus.

message.author: Chidi, manager
message.text: Sit with Ife as she prepares a handover. Bring one observation to our check-in and we will shape your first goal together.

frames.outcome: Introductions connect to a meaningful piece of work.

frames.label: Progress
frames.heading: Day one becomes a supported month.
frames.body: Zainab and her manager agree an initial goal and follow-up. The welcome carries into an ongoing development conversation.

message.author: Zainab
message.text: My first goal is to document the handover steps with Ife. We will review the draft at next week's check-in.

frames.outcome: A clear first goal, with support and a review point.

manual.title: When the welcome lives in separate lists
manual.outcome: The new joiner must piece together the beginning.

title: A leave request should not become a chase.
intro: Follow an employee request through context, manager review and a visible response, with responsibility clear at every step.
prompt: Can I take leave next month once our handover is covered?

frames.label: Request
frames.heading: One clear starting point.
frames.body: Femi shares the proposed dates and a handover note. The request is ready for the responsible manager to review.

message.author: Femi
message.text: I'd like to request 12-16 October. I have suggested a handover with Kemi, subject to her availability.

frames.outcome: The request includes the context a reviewer needs.

frames.label: Clarify
frames.heading: A question reaches the right person.
frames.body: Sade checks the proposed coverage before deciding. Femi can see what is still needed rather than guessing at the delay.

message.author: Sade, manager
message.text: Please confirm Kemi's availability for the handover. I will review the request with our team schedule and leave policy.

frames.outcome: The next action is specific and visible.

frames.label: Review
frames.heading: The manager has the missing context.
frames.body: Femi confirms the handover. Sade reviews the request using the company's policy and operational needs before recording a decision.

message.author: Femi
message.text: Kemi has confirmed. I will prepare the handover notes before the requested dates.

frames.outcome: A responsible reviewer makes the decision with context.

frames.label: Respond
frames.activity: Sample decision visible to the employee
frames.heading: The answer completes the loop.
frames.body: In this example, Sade approves the request and confirms the handover expectation. Femi can see the outcome and next action.

message.author: Sade, manager
message.text: Approved for this sample request. Please share the handover notes with Kemi before your leave begins.

frames.outcome: The employee sees an answer, not just a submission.

manual.title: When everyday requests lose their owner
items: Dates sent in a private chat
Employee asks again for an answer
manual.outcome: Submission and resolution become separate conversations.

title: Turn a check-in into the next useful step.
intro: See how a first-time team lead and her manager connect a clear goal, honest feedback and a practical learning action.
prompt: How can I make our weekly handovers clearer for everyone?

frames.label: Agree
frames.activity: Manager and employee shape the goal
frames.heading: Start with useful progress.
frames.body: Abena and her manager choose a practical goal: a handover template the team can use and explain.

message.author: Kojo, manager
message.text: Let's define success as a template your team understands. Bring a draft to our check-in and we will test it together.

frames.outcome: The goal includes evidence, support and a review point.

frames.label: Discuss
frames.heading: Feedback becomes a real conversation.
frames.body: The draft is useful, but ownership is unclear. The manager separates the learning need from a judgement about Abena.

message.author: Abena
message.text: The team likes the structure. We still need a clearer way to show who owns each unfinished task.

frames.outcome: A specific observation leads to specific support.

frames.label: Practise
frames.heading: Development fits the work itself.
frames.body: Abena adds an owner field and practises the handover with her manager. The development action stays connected to her goal.

message.author: Kojo, manager
message.text: Let's practise with one unfinished task. Ask the next owner to explain what they will do before we finish.

frames.outcome: Learning has a practical task and an available coach.

frames.label: Reflect
frames.heading: Progress ends with another beginning.
frames.body: They review the revised template and agree to try it with the team. The next conversation has a clear purpose.

message.author: Abena
message.text: I'll use the revised template at our next handover and bring the team's questions to our follow-up.

frames.outcome: A development conversation produces a shared next commitment.

manual.title: When development waits for review season
items: Goal stored in a review document
Learning chosen from a separate list
Next check-in has no shared record
manual.outcome: The employee reconnects the goal, feedback and support.

title: Find the question behind an open role.
intro: Follow a workforce review from a broad hiring concern to a checked explanation and a named next action.
prompt: Why is the approved operations role still at interview stage?

frames.label: Frame
frames.heading: Ask about a role, not everything.
frames.body: Ebiye narrows the review to one approved role. The question is where it stands and who owns the next step.

message.author: Ebiye
message.text: Let's review this vacancy's approval, current stage and next responsible owner before describing it as a recruitment delay.

frames.outcome: The discussion starts with a specific, answerable question.

frames.label: Explore
frames.heading: The stage tells part of the story.
frames.body: The sample pipeline shows an interview completed but a panel review still open. Ebiye looks for the underlying evidence.

message.author: Ebiye
message.text: The role is not waiting for approval. Let's check whether the outstanding panel feedback explains the open review.

frames.outcome: The view points to a record worth checking.

frames.label: Validate
frames.activity: Finding checked with the record owner
frames.heading: Check before turning context into certainty.
frames.body: The panel coordinator confirms which contribution is missing. The team records an explanation without blaming the recruiter or candidate.

message.author: Chidi, panel coordinator
message.text: Yes, we still need the operations scorecard. I will follow up with its owner before arranging the decision discussion.

frames.outcome: A checked explanation replaces a broad assumption.

frames.label: Act
frames.heading: Leave the review with a next step.
frames.body: Chidi owns the missing contribution and Ebiye owns the follow-up review. The dashboard informs the action; people remain accountable.

message.author: Ebiye
message.text: Chidi will follow up on the scorecard. We will revisit the role after that contribution is ready, then agree the candidate update.

frames.outcome: A specific follow-up, without claiming the role is filled.

manual.title: When the review starts with disconnected reports
items: Interview status in a separate tracker
Meeting ends with an unassigned question
manual.outcome: The number arrives before its context.

title: A thoughtful draft. Still your conversation.
intro: Watch a scripted candidate follow-up become a reviewed draft, with missing details questioned and the final choice left to HR.
prompt: Draft a warm next-step message without promising an offer or inventing an interview date.

frames.label: Context
frames.heading: Give the draft a bounded task.
frames.body: Nneka chooses a sample follow-up. The role and next step are known; an interview time has not been agreed.

message.author: Nneka's instruction
message.text: Invite Amaka to discuss the next interview step. Ask for availability, keep it warm and do not imply an offer.

frames.outcome: The task has clear facts and explicit boundaries.

frames.label: Draft
frames.heading: A starting point appears for review.
frames.body: The prepared example acknowledges the conversation and asks for availability. Nothing is sent, and no hiring decision is made.

message.author: Brew sample draft
message.text: Hi Amaka, thank you for speaking with us about the operations manager role. Could you share your availability to discuss the next interview step?

frames.outcome: A reviewable draft, not an automatically sent message.

frames.label: Review
frames.heading: The human makes the draft better.
frames.body: Nneka checks the facts and tone, then adds room for Amaka to ask questions before confirming availability.

message.author: Nneka's revision
message.text: Hi Amaka, thank you for our conversation. Could you share your availability for the next interview step? Please also send any questions you would like us to clarify.

frames.outcome: The reviewer checks the facts and adds human context.

frames.label: Ready
frames.activity: Reviewed example kept as a draft
frames.heading: Ready for a person to choose.
frames.body: Nneka's revised example remains a draft. A live communication would need the appropriate permissions, approvals and delivery service.

message.author: Nneka
message.text: The wording is ready for our communication process. I still own the next step. This demonstration has not contacted Amaka.

frames.outcome: Human-reviewed wording. No autonomous action or live AI.

manual.title: When every message starts from a blank page
manual.outcome: The reviewer assembles the first draft from scratch.
